domain_segments.text: The "Cheers" system is being developed by "Wine Ha'Emek," a wine trading company, to manage key business operations, including inventory management, customer management, and order processing and delivery.
The sales staff are responsible for placing customer orders, with each order being assigned to a specific employee.

Orders can be categorized as either regular or urgent and include the following details: order number, order date, current status (in process, dispatched, delivered, paid, suspended, or canceled), shipment date, and the assigned employee's information (ID, name, phone number, office address, email, and employment start date).
The actual delivery of orders is managed by an external company, called "GalGalim," and falls outside the scope of the current system.
Orders may consist of multiple wines in different quantities.
To minimize delivery costs, customers can place joint orders.
In such cases, the system must track which wines and quantities have been ordered by each customer.
For each customer in an order, the system records their ID, name, phone number, delivery address, email, and the date of first contact with the company.
Company employees are allowed to order wines under the same conditions as regular customers.
Urgent orders are processed with priority and must be placed by a single customer to ensure prompt delivery.
When placing an urgent order, the priority level (a number between 1 and 5) and the expected delivery time must be specified.
Regular orders, on the other hand, allow multiple customers to combine their wine selections into a single order to minimize delivery costs.
In such cases, the system tracks the specific wines and quantities ordered by each customer, as well as the main customer who is responsible for the entire order.
For every customer included in an urgent or regular order, the system records their ID, name, phone number, delivery address, email, and the date of first contact with the company.
Company employees may also place orders under the same conditions as regular customers.
Only employees in the marketing department are authorized to update wine information and types.
All other employees will have view-only access.
For example, sales staff can browse available wines when placing orders for customers.
Each type of wine is identified by its name and serial number.
Examples of wine types include red, white, sparkling, fortified, rosé, and dessert wines.
Additional details for each wine type include food pairings; In addition to the name of the dish, up to 5 links (URLs) to possible recipes will be kept.

Marketing employees can also recommend occasions suitable for drinking each wine type, providing a general description of the occasion (e.g., marriage proposal, nature hike, cheese night), along with the season and location (indoor/outdoor).
At the start of each month, the system will receive XML data from another system, called "Gefen," regarding wine producers and the wines they produce.
Additionally, weekly updates will be provided on the quantity purchased (each wine is produced by a single manufacturer).
For each manufacturer, the system will store the full name, contact phone number, address, and email.
A unique automatic identifier is assigned to each new manufacturer.
For each wine, the system will capture the name, description, production year, price per bottle, sweetness level (dry, semi-dry, semi-sweet, sweet), and product image.
Wines are distinguished by their manufacturer number and catalog number.
Marketing staff will link wines to their types and can modify price details and product images.
Each wine is stored in a specific location (e.g., main refrigerator, cellar), and each storage location has a unique number and name.
The system tracks the number of bottles of each wine at each storage location (wines may be stored in multiple locations and a single location may store multiple wines).
As wines are sold only from available stock, inventory must be updated after each sale.

The "Cheers" system will also generate the following reports: (1) Unproductive Employees Report: Generated by a sales employee, this report takes a time period as a parameter and displays the personal information of employees who placed fewer than 2 urgent orders OR fewer than 4 regular orders within that period; (2) Current Inventory Report by Wine: This report provides the inventory levels of all wines and is sent to the Gefen system in JSON format every weekend to assist with restocking preparations; (3) Wine Recommendation Report for Customers: Produced by a sales employee, this report returns a list of available wines that match the customer's preferences based on food, occasion, and wine type.

templates_in_scope.description: An actor represents a role that interacts with the use case within the system.
A use case represents a functional requirement of the system, defining interactions between an actor and the system.
An association between an actor and a use case demonstrates that the actor participates in the use case.
An include relationship between two use cases indicates that behavior of the included use case is inserted into the base use case.
An extend relationship implies that the behavior of the extending use case can be inserted into the base use case under certain conditions.
A generalization relationship between use cases where the child use case inherits the behavior and meaning of the parent use case.
A generalization relationship between actors where the child actor role inherits the behavior and responsibility of the parent actor role.
A system boundary defines the scope of the system for the use case under consideration.
